title: NodeBB Patches Eight AI-Found Flaws Exposing Admin Access and Private Chats
summary: Eight security flaws in NodeBB went public on Wednesday, along with the code to exploit them. Aikido Security rates all eight as high severity and says its AI pentest agents found them in a six-hour review of the forum software's source code.
card_summary: Eight security flaws in NodeBB went public on Wednesday, along with the code to exploit them. Aikido Security rates all eight as high severity and says its AI pentest agents found them in a six-hour review of the forum software's source code.

sections.impact:
Every version before 4.14.0 is affected.

Assessed severity: HIGH.
sections.mitigation: NodeBB has fixed them all, and administrators should be on 4.14.2.

email_summary: Eight security flaws in NodeBB went public on Wednesday, along with the code to exploit them. Severity is rated high.

title: Kimi K3 Agents Found Redis Zero-Days and Built RCE Exploit, Researchers Say
summary: Redis shipped seven security releases on July 23 after researchers published authenticated RCE PoCs for stock Redis 6.2.22, 7.4.9, 8.6.4, and 8.8.0.
card_summary: Redis shipped seven security releases on July 23 after researchers published authenticated RCE PoCs for stock Redis 6.2.22, 7.4.9, 8.6.4, and 8.8.0.

sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.

title: Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes
summary: A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client.
card_summary: A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client.

sections.impact:
The payload goes after the last 90 days of email, the organization's entire email directory, the password saved in the browser and the codes kept for two-factor recovery.

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.

email_summary: A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client. Severity is rated critical.
